explanation: A soft-deleted message moves to the user's Recoverable Items folder and is kept for the deleted item retention period. Hard delete marks messages for permanent removal instead.

stem: An analyst resolves a Defender XDR incident and adds a resolution note. What happens to the incident's active alerts?
explanation: Resolving an incident also resolves all the linked and active alerts in it, and the note appears in the activity log and details panel.
options: They move to a new incident

stem: Contoso still runs Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal. What has Microsoft announced for after March 31, 2027?
explanation: After March 31, 2027, Sentinel is no longer supported in the Azure portal and customers are redirected to the Microsoft Defender portal. Workspaces and data stay in place.
options: Sentinel moves to the Purview portal
The Azure portal gets a read-only mode
Sentinel is available only in Defender

stem: A threat hunter wants to run Python and Spark over months of lake data to build a custom anomaly model. What should the hunter use?
explanation: Notebooks, through the Microsoft Sentinel extension for Visual Studio Code, run Python and Spark jobs over data lake tables, which suits custom machine learning. Analytics rules and workbooks use KQL and cannot run Python.

stem: A tag should be added to incidents whenever an analyst raises their severity. Which automation rule condition can detect this?
explanation: The When incident is updated trigger supports state-change conditions such as changed, changed from and changed to. A creation condition checks only the state when the incident first appears.
options: Alert created by an NRT rule

stem: The CISO asks whether any open incidents in the tenant are linked to a threat that a threat analytics report tracks. Where can the analyst see this directly?
explanation: Each threat analytics report lists the related incidents in your tenant that are linked to the threat. The Action center shows remediation actions, not threat links.

stem: An engineer creates a new table to hold logs from an in-house app sent through the Logs Ingestion API. Which name will the table have?
explanation: Custom log tables end in _CL. The _KQL_CL suffix marks tables that KQL jobs create, and _SRCH marks search job results.

stem: A custom detection rule should act on the accounts in its results. Which two user actions need a security identifier (SID) column, such as AccountSid, in the query results? (Choose two.)
explanation: Disable user and Reset user authentication both need the SID from AccountSid, InitiatingProcessAccountSid, RequestAccountSid or OnPremSid. Mark user as compromised uses the object ID columns, and the device actions use DeviceId.

stem: An analyst wants every onboarded device to block a malicious file by its SHA-256 hash, even on devices where it has not been seen yet. What should the analyst do from the file page?
explanation: Adding a file indicator with a block action stops the file from running on all devices in scope, including ones where it has not appeared. Stop and quarantine acts only on devices where the file was seen.
options: Add an indicator to block it

stem: An analyst renamed an incident to describe the attack. Later, another incident is merged into it. What happens to the custom name?
explanation: When another incident is merged into a renamed incident, Defender gives the incident a new name and overwrites the custom one, so key context belongs in tags or comments too.
options: It is added to the tags
It is kept with no change
Defender gives it a new name

stem: In the Email summary panel, which action is available in Threat Explorer but not in Real-time detections?
explanation: Go hunt is available only in Threat Explorer. Email preview, the header view and the email entity page are available from the summary panel in both tools, with preview needing the Preview role.

stem: To let Sentinel's service account run playbooks in a resource group, someone must grant it the Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor role there. Which role does that person need?
explanation: Granting the service account its permissions needs Owner or User Access Administrator on the resource group. Sentinel Contributor can attach playbooks to rules but cannot assign roles.

stem: An analyst enabled Microsoft Graph activity logs 20 minutes ago and sees no rows yet for a suspicious app's recent calls. What is the most likely reason?
explanation: In most regions Graph activity log events arrive within 30 minutes, and some take up to 2 hours, so recent calls may not show yet. The feature needs an Entra ID P1 or P2 license, not Audit (Premium).
options: Events can take up to 2 hours
Logs are kept for one day only

stem: A security admin wants analysts to use the hunting graph and blast radius in the Defender portal. What must the tenant have in place?
explanation: Microsoft Sentinel graph powers the hunting graph and blast radius, and it is provisioned through the Sentinel data lake onboarding. Fusion and live response are unrelated features.
options: Live response turned on for servers
Onboarding to the Sentinel data lake
A Defender for Cloud Apps policy

stem: The SOC optimization overview shows threat-based coverage as Medium for a scenario. What does that mean?
explanation: Coverage is High above 75% of the rules Microsoft recommends, Medium from 30% to 74%, and Low below 30%. It compares active analytics rules, not table use.
options: Under 30% of recommended rules are on
30% to 74% of recommended rules are on
Half of the ingested data tables are unused
Over 75% of recommended rules are on

stem: An analyst bookmarked hunting results and has now confirmed the activity is malicious. What should the analyst do next in Microsoft Sentinel?
explanation: A bookmark can be promoted to a new incident or added to an existing one, so the evidence moves into the incident workflow. Deleting the query would lose the hunt logic for later use.
options: Export the bookmark to a notebook
Create an incident from the bookmark
Add the bookmark to a watchlist
Promote the bookmark to an analytics rule

stem: Fabrikam must remove a column holding personal data from incoming events before they are stored, to meet a privacy rule. Where should this be done?
explanation: A transformation in the data collection rule runs at ingestion, so it can drop or mask columns before data is stored. Queries after ingestion cannot remove data already written.
options: A KQL job on the data lake

stem:
A scheduled Microsoft Sentinel rule uses this query:

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{SigninLogs}\\\texttt{| where ResultType == "50126"}\\\texttt{| summarize Failures = count() by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress}\\\texttt{| where Failures > 20}\end{array}$$

What does each row the query returns represent?
explanation: summarize counts failed sign-ins per pair of user and IP address, and the final where keeps only pairs with more than 20 failures. A user who failed 25 times spread across several addresses would not appear unless one address passed 20.
options: A user with 20 failures from any IP
An IP address used by 20 users
A user and IP pair over 20 failures
One failed sign-in for one user

stem: An analyst needs to know what a never-before-seen executable does when it runs, including network calls and files it drops, without running it on a production device. Which file page action helps?
explanation: Deep analysis runs the file in a secure cloud environment and reports its behavior, such as network activity and dropped files. Downloading the file only gets a copy that someone would still have to detonate.

stem: An internal Teams group chat at Contoso receives a message later identified as malware, and two of the five recipients are excluded from ZAP for Teams protection. What does ZAP do?
explanation: Teams chats share one copy of a message, so ZAP blocks it for everyone in the chat unless every recipient is excluded. Only when all recipients are excluded does ZAP take no action.

stem: Two automation rules match a new incident and a change one makes then fires a third, update-trigger rule. Put the runs in order:
explanation: Rules for the incident creation trigger all run first, by their order numbers, and only then do rules with the update trigger run. Each trigger type keeps its own queue.

stem: A hunter wants the 10 devices with the highest count of alerts. Which operator returns those rows, ordered by the count?
explanation: top returns the first N rows sorted by the given column, so it gives the highest counts. take and limit return any 10 rows with no ordering.

stem: A Defender XDR incident joins a phishing email, a malicious file on an endpoint and lateral movement to a server. Which part of the incident page lays out the alerts in order with a graph of the entities?
explanation: The attack story shows the alerts in sequence beside an incident graph of the users, devices and other entities involved. The evidence list and assets tab list items without the sequence, and the activity log records changes to the incident.

stem: An analyst wants to tie each Microsoft Graph request in MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs to the sign-in that issued its token. Which column should she join to UniqueTokenIdentifier in the sign-in tables?
explanation: SignInActivityId in the Graph logs matches UniqueTokenIdentifier in the sign-in log tables. RequestId and OperationId identify the request or batch, not the sign-in.

stem: Match each need to the Microsoft Sentinel storage choice that fits:
explanation: The Analytics tier supports alerting, hunting and workbooks; the Data lake tier is cold, cheap storage reached through jobs; and Defender XDR data sits in the XDR default tier for 30 days.
rows: Real-time analytics rules and hunting
Low-cost retention for compliance
Default advanced hunting for 30 days

stem: An analyst building a Security Copilot agent wants it to return a verdict on a suspicious URL by reasoning over the organization's own security data. Which Sentinel MCP capability fits?
explanation: The entity analyzer tools in the data exploration collection retrieve and reason over lake data to give a verdict on entities such as URLs and users. The agent creation tools help build agents but do not analyze the entity themselves.

stem: An engineer wants diagnostic logs from an Azure Key Vault sent to Microsoft Sentinel. What should be configured on the Key Vault?
explanation: Azure resource logs are sent by a diagnostic setting on the resource that targets the Log Analytics workspace, and Azure Policy can apply such settings at scale. Agents are only for machines.
options: The Azure Monitor Agent on the vault itself
A diagnostic setting to the workspace

stem: Put the steps for creating a custom detection rule in Microsoft Defender XDR in order:
explanation: The rule wizard moves from the query to alert details, then enrichment such as dynamic titles and entity mapping, then automated actions, then the device scope, and finally review. The rule runs as soon as it is created.
options: Review and turn on the rule

stem: Automatic attack disruption contained a business-critical device during a ransomware incident. The analyst has confirmed remediation is in place. What should the analyst do next?
explanation: Attack disruption leaves the SOC in control of bringing assets back online, so once remediation is confirmed the analyst releases the device. Turning off attack disruption would remove protection for future incidents.

stem: Match each task in a Microsoft Sentinel deployment to the role built for it:
explanation: Playbook Operator runs playbooks, Logic App Contributor edits Consumption logic apps, and Automation Contributor is the role the Sentinel service account uses for automation rules. Responder manages incidents.
rows: Run a playbook manually
Create and edit a Consumption playbook
Let automation rules run playbooks
Manage incidents and view data

stem:
A hunter runs this query:

$$\begin{array}{l}\texttt{DeviceNetworkInfo}\\\texttt{| mv-expand IP = parse\_json(IPAddresses)}\\\texttt{| extend Address = tostring(IP.IPAddress)}\\\texttt{| project DeviceName, Address}\end{array}$$

Why is mv-expand needed?
explanation: IPAddresses holds a JSON array, and mv-expand turns each element into its own row so each address can be read and projected. Removing duplicates would need distinct or summarize.
options: It joins the array to another table
It makes one row per array item
It converts the array to text

stem: Defender for Cloud Apps raises Unusual file download (by user). The analyst finds that the user's OneDrive client was syncing to an approved external backup. How should the alert be handled?
explanation: A sync with approved backup software is a false positive for this detection, so the alert is dismissed. Suspending or marking the user compromised is the response to a true positive.
options: Dismiss it as a false positive
Revoke every OAuth app it uses
